title: [CQ-C03b] Read-only MCP stdio analyzer client
description:
Objective: a minimal, bounded MCP stdio client the daemon can use to query an external read-only analyzer (CQ-C03's Serena). The daemon has no MCP client library today; its dependencies are chokidar, pino and ws.

Split out of CQ-C03 (task-8d009716) by architect-e4b7eee0 on 2026-10-29, as a size split.

Interface (CQ-C03 plans against these exact names):
- New module packages/moe-daemon/src/context/mcpStdioClient.ts.
- `export interface AnalyzerLaunch { readonly command: string; readonly args: readonly string[]; readonly cwd: string; readonly env: Readonly<Record<string, string>>; readonly timeoutMs: number; readonly maxResponseBytes: number }`.
- `export interface AnalyzerServerInfo { readonly name: string; readonly version: string; readonly protocolVersion: string }`.
- `export interface AnalyzerTool { readonly name: string; readonly inputSchema: unknown }`.
- `export type AnalyzerCallResult = { readonly ok: true; readonly text: string; readonly truncated: boolean } | { readonly ok: false; readonly reason: string }`.
- `export interface AnalyzerSession { readonly server: AnalyzerServerInfo; readonly tools: readonly AnalyzerTool[]; call(tool: string, args: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>): Promise<AnalyzerCallResult>; close(): Promise<void> }`.
- `export type AnalyzerOpenResult = { readonly ok: true; readonly session: AnalyzerSession } | { readonly ok: false; readonly reason: string }`.
- `export async function openAnalyzerSession(launch: AnalyzerLaunch, allowedTools: readonly string[]): Promise<AnalyzerOpenResult>`. A malformed launch or allowlist throws invalidInput before any spawn. Every child, protocol or timeout failure returns a reason and never throws.

Rules:
- Spawning: no shell; env is EXACTLY launch.env, with nothing inherited.
- Framing: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 per the MCP stdio transport.
- Handshake: initialize with a protocolVersion and clientInfo {name 'moe-daemon'}, then validate serverInfo.name, serverInfo.version and the result's protocolVersion as non-empty strings, then send notifications/initialized.
- tools/list: follow nextCursor up to a fixed page cap.
- call():
  - Refuses a tool that is not in allowedTools, or not listed, WITHOUT sending: reasons 'tool-not-allowed' and 'tool-not-listed'.
  - Concatenates the result's text content items. isError:true gives { ok: false, reason: 'tool-error' }.
  - A response line over maxResponseBytes fails the session with 'response-too-large'.
- Deadlines: one per request (timeoutMs), with 'timeout'. Process exit fails every pending call with 'exited:<code|signal>'.
- Protocol: a malformed line or a mismatched id gives 'protocol-violation'. Server notifications are ignored. Server-to-client requests get JSON-RPC error -32601.
- stderr is drained and capped, and never parsed.
- close() ends stdin, waits at most 2 s, then kills the WHOLE process tree: POSIX via a detached process group and a negative-pid kill; Windows via `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F`. An analyzer may spawn language servers.

Scope boundaries: the client and its regression tests only, driven by fake MCP server fixtures in tests. No Serena-specific logic, no activation, no MCP tool registration. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout (2026-10-24). Never directly edit .moe.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test
definitionOfDone: Against a fake stdio MCP server, the client completes initialize, notifications/initialized and paged tools/list, exposes serverInfo name, version and protocolVersion plus each tool's inputSchema, and returns call() text for an allowed, listed tool.

A non-allowlisted or unlisted tool is refused without any frame reaching the server. Malformed lines, mismatched ids, oversize responses, server requests, a hang (timeout), a crash or an exit each give the documented reason with no throw, and each has a named test.

close() and every failure path kill the whole process tree: a fake server that spawns a grandchild leaves no live process afterwards on POSIX. A Windows taskkill path is covered by a platform-gated test or a recorded native run. The child gets exactly launch.env.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0, and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

1. Tree kill on every failure path:
   - fail() kills by default, which covers timeout, protocol-violation, response-too-large, reject() and a spawn error (no pid: no-op).
   - The exit handler group-kills once. It is now pinned by S14 (kill recorded BEFORE close(), and close() adds none) and by S15 (crash: the grandchild is gone before close()).
   - close() kills; an open failure awaits close().
   - win32: a self-crashed root's orphans are unreachable (documented limit).
2. Env: exactly launch.env on POSIX (S5); the libuv superset on win32 (documented).
3. A refused tool sends no frame: the allowlist and listed checks run before request() (S6).
4. Buffers:
   - stdout partial line capped at 4 MiB (S7 huge);
   - stdin reply backlog capped (S7 flood);
   - stderr is 'ignore';
   - tools/list bounded at 16 pages, now pinned by S16.
5. No stream-handler throw can escape:
   - JSON.parse and the fatal UTF-8 decode run inside try;
   - only a string or finite id is echoed (S7 deepid);
   - process.kill runs inside try;
   - a write after end surfaces as stdin 'error', which is handled;
   - execFile errors go to its callback.
6. Test determinism:
   - S14: killTree is synchronous inside the 'exit' handler, so it runs before the call's promise continuation.
   - S16 == 16: the fake logs each line before it replies, and the client sends no 17th request.
   - S15, like S11 and S12, relies on init reaping the SIGKILLed grandchild. The Dockerfile runs no tests.
7. Theoretical, noted for CQ-C03:
   - inputSchema is raw server JSON, nested to any depth inside a 4 MiB line. A consumer that JSON.stringify()s it outside a try could hit a RangeError, so treat it as untrusted.
   - After a fail-time kill, the exit handler signals -pid again, at the reap instant. This is the documented "once at exit" design; pid reuse within that tick would need pid wrap.
8. No forbidden-pattern tokens (grep). No .moe edits. Git use was read-only (diff, archive, show, rev-parse, ls-files).

implementationPlan.description:
Implement packages/moe-daemon/src/context/mcpStdioClient.ts, exporting EXACTLY the names and shapes in this row's description: AnalyzerLaunch, AnalyzerServerInfo, AnalyzerTool, AnalyzerCallResult, AnalyzerSession, AnalyzerOpenResult and openAnalyzerSession. CQ-C03 (task-8d009716) is already planned against them. One additive export: MCP_FRAME_LIMIT_BYTES = 4 MiB.

1. Validation: synchronous, before any spawn, throwing invalidInput from util/errors.ts. Snapshot-copy every field first, so later caller mutation is inert.
- command: an absolute path (path.isAbsolute) with no NUL. On Windows, libuv runs <cwd>\name.exe before PATH, and cwd here is analyzer-controlled repository content (mem gotcha-windows-libuv-spawn-searches-cwd-first).
- args: an array of at most 256 strings, none containing NUL.
- cwd: absolute.
- env: a plain object. Keys are non-empty and contain no '=' or NUL; values are strings with no NUL.
- timeoutMs: an integer from 1 to 600000.
- maxResponseBytes: an integer from 1 to MCP_FRAME_LIMIT_BYTES.
- allowedTools: 1 to 64 unique non-empty strings.

2. Spawn: spawn(command, args, {cwd, env: copy, stdio: ['pipe','pipe','ignore'], shell: false, windowsHide: true, detached: platform !== 'win32'}).
- detached gives POSIX a process group.
- stderr 'ignore' is the strongest drain-and-cap: no pipe can fill and stall the child, and nothing is parsed.
- A synchronous throw (Windows .cmd/.bat EINVAL) or an 'error' event gives {ok:false, reason:`spawn-failed:${code}`}.
- Attach child.stdin.on('error', noop) BEFORE any write (mem gotcha-local-runner-execfile-stdin).

3. Framing:
- Split stdout on 0x0A at the Buffer level.
- If the partial line would exceed MCP_FRAME_LIMIT_BYTES, fail the session with 'response-too-large' immediately, without waiting for a newline, so memory stays bounded.
- Strip one trailing 0x0D. The Python MCP SDK in Serena 1.6.2 (mcp 1.28.1) writes through a TextIOWrapper, which emits CRLF on Windows.
- Skip empty lines.
- Decode with TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true}), then JSON.parse. A failure, a non-object, an array (batch) or jsonrpc !== '2.0' is 'protocol-violation'.
- Classify each message:
  - method plus id: a server request. Reply with result {} for 'ping' and with error {code: -32601, message: 'Method not found'} for anything else.
  - method without id: a notification, ignored.
  - Otherwise a response. Its id must be a pending numeric id, and it must have exactly one of an object 'result' or an 'error' object with an integer code. Anything else is 'protocol-violation'.

4. Session state:
- The first failure wins.
- 'protocol-violation', 'response-too-large' and 'timeout' are session-fatal: kill the tree at once (no grace period), and resolve every pending request with that reason.
- The child's 'exit' event gives `exited:${code ?? signal}` unless a failure was already set.
- Requests after a failure or a close return {ok:false, reason} without writing.
- A per-request deadline of timeoutMs uses an unref'd timer that is cleared on settle.

5. Handshake:
- Send initialize with {protocolVersion: '2025-06-18', capabilities: {}, clientInfo: {name: 'moe-daemon', version: VERSION from util/version.ts}}. '2025-06-18' is in Serena's mcp SUPPORTED list, and the daemon's own server speaks 2024-11-05.
- The result needs non-empty protocolVersion, serverInfo.name and serverInfo.version strings, each at most 256 chars. Expose the server's protocolVersion as returned.
- Then send notifications/initialized.
- tools/list: follow a string nextCursor for at most 16 pages. Every tool needs a non-empty name of at most 256 chars and a plain-object inputSchema, which is kept as parsed.
- Exceeding the page cap, a duplicate name or a bad shape is 'protocol-violation'.
- A JSON-RPC error answer during open gives `rpc-error:${code}`.
- Any open failure kills the tree before returning {ok:false, reason}.

6. call(tool, args):
- A non-string tool, or args that are not a plain object or not JSON-serializable, rejects with invalidInput (caller shape).
- Then, in order, each refused WITHOUT writing: 'tool-not-allowed', 'tool-not-listed', then the session reason.
- Send tools/call {name, arguments}.
- A JSON-RPC error gives `rpc-error:${code}`; the session continues.
- isError === true gives 'tool-error'; the session continues.
- content must be an array, else 'protocol-violation' (fatal). The text is the '' concatenation of items with type 'text' and a string text; other items are skipped.
- When the text exceeds maxResponseBytes UTF-8 bytes, cut it at a character boundary with node:string_decoder (StringDecoder.write of the byte prefix never splits a character) and set truncated: true. maxResponseBytes caps the ANSWER, which is what C03's T8 'response-byte-cap' expects. MCP_FRAME_LIMIT_BYTES caps every LINE, including a large tools/list.

7. close(): idempotent, and returns the same promise on every call.
- Pending requests resolve 'closed'.
- POSIX: end stdin, wait at most 2 s for exit, then ALWAYS process.kill(-pid, 'SIGKILL'). The group can outlive the leader, for example language servers. ESRCH is ignored.
- win32: run `<SystemRoot>\System32\taskkill.exe /PID <pid> /T /F` FIRST, while the root is alive, because a root that has exited orphans its children out of /T's reach. Use an absolute path, execFile, a 5 s timeout and windowsHide, and ignore errors. Then end stdin.
- Both: wait at most 2 s for 'exit', then child.kill('SIGKILL') as a last resort.
- Failure paths use the same tree kill without the graceful wait.

Error handling: every child, protocol, IO or timeout failure becomes a reason string with a fixed code and never includes analyzer bytes. Only caller shape throws. No timer or listener survives close.
implementationPlan.note: Implemented context/mcpStdioClient.ts with the exact row API + MCP_FRAME_LIMIT_BYTES (4 MiB). tsc --noEmit exit 0 in Linux snapshot /tmp/moe-c03b.6syuqa (HEAD 7c7ce76 + overlay). Additions within plan intent: on win32 the command must also match ^(drive:\\|UNC) because path.win32.isAbsolute accepts root-relative '\\x'; call() snapshots args via a JSON round trip, so the sent frame equals the validated value; the child 'exit' fail path also runs the tree kill (POSIX group SIGKILL reaches orphans; win32 skips a dead root, the documented limitation). Finding for step 2: libuv on Windows copies required vars (SYSTEMROOT, PATH, TEMP, USERPROFILE, ...) into any explicit env block that lacks them, so 'exactly launch.env' cannot hold on Windows; S5 asserts exact on POSIX and launch.env ⊆ child env with extras ⊆ libuv's required list on win32. Shared tree has many unrelated dirty paths from other sessions; none touched.

Tests S1-S13 (24 cases) in context/mcpStdioClient.test.ts, all green in the Linux snapshot (node v24.21.0). Mutation proof on a scratch snapshot copy, against the FINAL compacted runtime (all red where expected): skip the allowlist → S6 red; inherit process.env → S5 red; drop the partial-line bound → S7 huge red; drop the group kill → S12 + S11 + S7 garbage/badid/huge/hang red (on POSIX it is the only failure-path kill); no server-request reply → S8 red; drop the CR strip → S2 red (better than the plan's 'none': the crlf fixture also writes a blank CRLF line, which parses as '\r' without the strip); drop the StringDecoder cut → S3 red. Deviations: (1) S10 proves 'nothing spawned' with a passthrough vi.fn spy on node:child_process spawn (deterministic) instead of a marker file plus a wait; (2) S7 hang uses timeoutMs 1500, not 300, because the deadline also covers initialize, and node cold start on Windows can pass 300 ms; (3) S5 is exact on POSIX; on win32 it asserts launch.env ⊆ child env with any extras ⊆ libuv's required list (libuv make_program_env copies them in). Runtime was also compacted: 271 lines runtime + 199 test = 470 total (see step 3 on size).
